_rule: EVERY ELEMENT IS MATCHED IN POSITION, SIZE, PROPORTION, WEIGHT, COLOUR AND DENSITY - WHILE EVERY STROKE STAYS OUR OWN DRAWING, NEVER TRACED.
_what_this_is: One reconciled, buildable specification of the paper-bomb reference, assembled from three independent metrology passes plus a fourth verification pass run for this document. Numbers only. No pixel of either guide was traced, sampled, masked, thresholded into a shipped asset or written anywhere a build can read it.

_conventions.origin: the TAG's top-left virtual corner - the intersection of the fitted top and left edge lines, i.e. the corner the chamfer cuts off. x right, y down.
_conventions.units: fractions of the tag's own width W and height H, and millimetres on the shipped 70.0 x 156.0 mm card (fW x 70, fH x 156)
_conventions.tag_edge: located at the HALF-MAXIMUM of the paper-to-background transition in warmth (R minus B), which separates cream paper and red ink from the neutral white background and its neutral drop shadow. Stable to +-0.13% on the tag rect across thresholds from 0.25 to 0.80 of the paper level.
_conventions.ours_tag_edge: NOT detected. Taken from the atlas plan, which is exact: the front island's card (0,0) is at atlas pixel (16, 16) at 12.923 px/mm, so the card is 904.61 x 2015.99 px. This removes the +-0.3 mm that a soft texture-island edge put on every earlier OURS number.
_conventions.colour: STORED file values, sRGB-encoded 0..1 (read with colorspace Non-Color, which returns the stored 8-bit value). Linear values are named as such.
_conventions.binarisation: red classified FIRST, then black. A deep seal red is darker than any sensible black threshold, so classifying black first loses it between the two masks.
_conventions.authority: V1 for every proportion, stroke, ornament and colour; V2 for the identity and placement of the text and for the size of the real-kanji blocks.

_sources.V2: References/PaperBomb/paperbomb_guide_v2_real_glyphs.png (300 x 653; tag 274.30 x 635.89 px at 3.919 / 4.076 px/mm)

_sources.rectification: None needed. V1's four edges are within 0.013 deg of axis-aligned (fit rms 0.016-0.049 px) and V2's within 0.030 deg (rms 0.013-0.022 px). No rotation or keystone correction was applied to either; the tag rectangle was taken from robust line fits to the four straight edge runs and measurements were made in each image's native pixels.

rows.reference_V1: paper stored #F6E6C6 (0.9647,0.9020,0.7765) = linear (0.9216,0.7914,0.5647), luma 0.803; black core stored #0F100D (0.059,0.063,0.051) = linear luma 0.0047; contrast 170:1 on the ink median, 244:1 on its darkest quartile
rows.reference_V2: paper #F6E5C3, black #0C0D0A, contrast ~200:1 (V2's 2.2x downsample pushes the surviving core pixels darker - V1 is the conservative figure)
rows.adopted_value_mm: paper linear (0.9216,0.7914,0.5647) luma 0.803; black linear luma 0.0047; contrast 170:1
rows.tolerance: contrast ratio within a factor of 1.5 of the adopted target; paper luma +-4%; black core luma within a factor of 2
rows.ours: paper stored (0.8549,0.7922,0.6588) = linear luma 0.597; black core stored (0.2471,0.2431,0.2392) = linear luma 0.0470; contrast 11.7:1. Minimum, p0.1 and p1 of our black are ALL exactly 0.2400 stored - the black is clamped flat on the floor with no dark tail at all.
rows.delta: -93% on contrast (11.7:1 against 170:1). Paper is 26% dark; black is 10x light.
rows.how_to_achieve: This is the one row that is a POLICY decision, not a drawing error. The module deliberately clamps every channel at DIELECTRIC_FLOOR_LINEAR = 0.0473 (stored 0.235 = 60/255) and says so in its own comment. Three steps, in order of how free they are: (a) raise PALETTE.paper from (0.700,0.587,0.393) to the band ceiling (0.870,0.747,0.533) - free, inside the stated band, buys 11.7:1 -> 16:1; (b) lower the floor from 60/255 to 30/255 (linear 0.0137), which is the figure most PBR authoring guides actually cite for non-metal albedo, and set black_wet to (0.0140,0.0137,0.0130) - buys ~55:1; (c) drop the floor for ink only and use the measured (0.0048,0.0047,0.0045) - reaches ~161:1 and matches the guide. ASK THE USER before (b) or (c): it changes a shipped-asset standard they wrote down on purpose.
rows.expected_visual_effect: The whole card stops reading grey-on-tan and starts reading black-on-cream. Nothing else on this list changes the read at every viewing distance the way this does, and no amount of extra coverage compensates for it.
rows.confidence: high on the measurement (three independent passes agree to 3/255); the remedy is a judgement call

rows.ours: FIVE components: body 31.26x44.18 (476 mm2), radical 11.76x32.58 (116 mm2), an orphan flick 6.27x8.28 at (12.3..18.5, 75.1..83.3), and two strokes broken out of the body at (47.7..54.4, 92.2..97.8) and (44.0..49.6, 85.2..91.8). Cap the erosion so no hole may sever a stroke: after breaking the glyph up, run a connected-component check and re-bridge anything that detaches. measure.py already has the hooks for a component count - make it a build gate (fail if the centre glyph is more than 2 components).

rows.element: Border frame - number of rules per side

rows.reference_V2: exactly ONE rule per side - same profile shape

rows.tolerance: no second peak above 0.15 occupancy anywhere in the 0..12 mm border band
rows.ours: left 2 (a 0.08 mm hairline at 3.41 mm plus the main rule at 4.06 mm), right 1, top 3 (6.58 mm at occupancy 1.00, a 7.16 mm shoulder, and a SECOND FULL-WIDTH rule at 9.56 mm at occupancy 1.00), bottom 2 (7.39 mm at 1.00 and a weaker one at 10.41 mm)
rows.delta: one extra full-width rule top and bottom, 2.98 mm inside the outer one, plus a left hairline
rows.how_to_achieve: Set inner_rule_sides = (). Keep bracket_leg_* - the reference does carry a doubled line at the corners, it just never runs the length of the edge. Then chase the 3.41 mm left hairline, which is a second pass of the outer rule, not a designed line.
rows.expected_visual_effect: A double frame against a single one changes the whole read of the card at thumbnail size and is the reason ours looks printed where the guide looks brushed.
rows.confidence: high - confirmed by all three passes and by a red-occupancy profile here

v1_v2_adjudication.why: V1 sits 0.43% off the shipped 70x156 card (0.44872); V2 is 3.87% off, i.e. stretched 3.9% vertically per unit width. Both figures are stable to +-0.13% across binarisation thresholds from 0.25 to 0.80 of the paper level, so this is a real difference between the two files, not a measurement choice. Use V1 for every proportion and every millimetre conversion. NOTE: an earlier pass reported V1 at 0.44887 ('the card to 0.03%') on a tag rect 6 px wider than any threshold in that sweep reproduces; that claim does not survive.

The widths agree to 1.3%. The height difference is exactly V2's own 3.9% vertical rescale (57.21 x 1.039 = 59.4). V1 is the one that lands correctly on a 70x156 card.
x agrees to 0.15 mm - both put the ring on the tag's vertical midline. The 2.6 mm y difference is more than V2's stretch explains, so V2's content also drifted; V1's y is the one to build to.

Agreement to 1% on a metric that is usually fragile. Both say a fifth of the ring's own envelope is bare paper.

They agree on w/h to 1.6% and on width-as-a-fraction-of-the-tag to 1.5%. Take V1 for the absolute size; the shared conclusion - the character is WIDER than it is tall and spans 84% of the card - holds either way.

Agreement to 2/255 on every channel and 0.35 deg of hue. Settled.
V2 is 3/255 darker because its downsample pushed the surviving core pixels toward the stroke centres. Both say a near-neutral near-black, not a charcoal. V1 is the conservative target.

Every V2 figure here sits at or past its own 1.96 cycles/mm Nyquist limit, so it measures the downsample rather than the artwork. V2 must not be used for any fine-texture statistic: fibre, kasure hole size, stroke-edge wavelength or bleed width.
Both are flat, evenly lit sheets. There is no fold shading to match.

not_capturable_as_a_number: Brush GESTURE - the sense that a hand moved. Measurable proxies: stroke-width modulation within one stroke (the reference's centre glyph runs 22.6:1 from its thinnest filament to its widest belly, and that is a LOWER bound because 22.6 is floored by V1's own pixel grid; ours is 3.4:1), and the wet-to-dry taper along a lap. Neither proxy guarantees the gesture.
The RHYTHM of the flame's tongues - thin, thick, thin, thick, thin (1.79, 6.16, 1.46, 6.50, 1.57 mm). The widths are measurable; whether the alternation reads as a flame is not.

Whether the pseudo-glyph columns in V1 should have influenced our composition at all. They are not characters, so their extent (63.7 mm tall, 8.9 mm wide) is not a target - but the DENSITY they give the upper third of the card is a real design fact that the real kanji have to carry instead.
Whether V1's lower-LEFT pseudo-glyph mark group (x 7.28..15.90, y 100.07..114.11 mm) should be reinstated as something. V2 drops it; we do not have it. That is a design call, not a metrology one.
How much wear is right. Both guides are clean, evenly aged sheets. Ours is a used prop. The spec targets the guides; the product may legitimately want more. Decide once, deliberately.
Whether the 0.43% aspect difference between V1 and the shipped 70 x 156 card matters. It is 0.3 mm on a 70 mm width. The card's dimensions are a product decision; the guide is a picture.

human_judgement.question: Does the 爆 read as ONE character?
human_judgement.how_to_judge: Numbers can count components and measure gaps, but only an eye can say whether the 火 radical reads as part of the character or as a blot beside it. Look at the card at thumbnail size (about 40 px tall) and at 100%. At thumbnail size the radical and the body should merge into one mass; at 100% they should be clearly two strokes that nearly touch.

human_judgement.question: Does the ring read as ONE fast brush stroke?
human_judgement.how_to_judge: Hole fraction, thickness distribution and angular coverage can all be right while the ring still reads as a decorated circle. The test: trace the stroke with your eye and see whether you can tell where the brush started and where it ran out. In the reference the band thins into its own gap - it tapers at the end of the lap rather than bulging. Ours currently ends WETTER than it starts, which is why it reads directionless. Fix the direction, then judge the gesture by looking.

human_judgement.question: Is the dry-brush breakup believable, or does it look like noise?
human_judgement.how_to_judge: Our kasure holes are already the right size, shape and alignment - there are just too few. When you add more, the failure mode is speckle: holes scattered evenly like film grain instead of clustered where a splitting brush would leave them. Judge by covering the rest of the card and asking whether the voids follow the stroke.

human_judgement.question: Does the flame emblem sit above the character, or compete with it?
human_judgement.how_to_judge: This is a weight judgement that no single number captures. The reference's emblem is five delicate strokes; ours is one fat welded mass with 61% more ink in the same box. After thinning it, squint at the card: the eye should land on 爆 first, the ring second, the emblem third.

human_judgement.question: Do the corner ornaments look like craft or like decoration?
human_judgement.how_to_judge: The measurable part is the 2.1 mm outboard dart. The unmeasurable part is the hook: the reference's curls inboard like a comma turning down-and-in, with ink pooling darkest where the two rules cross. Draw it, then look at a 4x zoom of each corner as a buyer would in a product shot.

human_judgement.question: Is the ink DARK, or merely darker?
human_judgement.how_to_judge: The contrast ratio is arithmetic, but whether the card reads as black ink on cream paper is a look-at call, and it depends on the shader and the lighting as well as the albedo. Judge it in the shipped gallery render, not in the map. If the render still reads grey at 55:1, the floor decision needs revisiting again.

human_judgement.question: Is the red cinnabar or brick?
human_judgement.how_to_judge: Saturation 0.90 is the target, but the perceived hue shifts with the paper behind it. Put our red and the reference's side by side at the same size on the same background before accepting it.

human_judgement.question: Does the whole card balance?
human_judgement.how_to_judge: The reference is very slightly left- and bottom-weighted: the filled lower-left chop balances the sparser lower right. Ours currently leans the other way. After the size changes land, look at the card upside down and out of focus - the two lower quadrants should feel about equally heavy.

human_judgement.question: Is anything traced?
human_judgement.how_to_judge: Not a look-at test but a process test, and the one that protects the product. Every stroke must come out of paperbomb_art.py's own path generators. The module already refuses to open the guides (FORBIDDEN_INPUT_FRAGMENTS, GuideAccess, no_guide_access) - keep that gate, and keep this spec numeric. Matching a measured width is not tracing; sampling a pixel is.

already_correct_do_not_change: Border rule RECTANGLE. Ours is 61.836 x 142.033 mm centred (34.981, 77.594); V1's is 61.877 x 142.085 centred (34.971, 77.718). That is 0.04 mm on width, 0.05 mm on height and 0.12 mm on centre. Earlier advice to move the rules 0.5-0.8 mm outward came from comparing numbers measured against two different tag-edge conventions; on one convention the insets already agree to 0.15 mm. DO NOT MOVE THE RULES.
Flame emblem POSITION and WIDTH: ours (34.75, 30.41) x 23.29 mm wide against the reference's (34.83, 30.59) x 23.74. Correct to 0.2 mm and 0.45 mm. Only its ink weight and stroke count are wrong.

Lower text columns' horizontal placement: 焼尽 at x 56.7-57.8 mm against the reference's 57.3-57.6, and 瞬業 at 35.2 against 35.0. A blanket 'push the columns out' fix would break these. Only the UPPER pair is inboard.
Column PITCH: our advances are 14.7-16.1 mm against the reference's 12.7-15.9 mm. The pitch is right; the glyphs inside it are small.

Big seal FRAME and PANEL boxes in the spec: big_seal_frame_x (0.0827, 0.3387) = 5.79..23.71 mm and big_seal_panel_x (0.110, 0.310) = 7.70..21.70 mm are within 0.4 mm of the reference's 17.81 mm frame and 13.66 mm inner block.
Small seal FRAME box in the spec: small_seal_frame_* = 8.97 x 17.86 mm against the reference's 9.0 x 17.8 mm.
Bottom centreline red leaf: ours at (34.98, 151.91) 0.77 x 2.17 mm against V1's (35.05, 151.70) 0.80 x 2.60 mm.
Kasure hole SHAPE: 0.31 mm median diameter against 0.30, elongation 4.8 against 4.2, 88% of holes within 30 deg of the stroke tangent against 83% (random would be 33%). Only the COUNT is short.
Ink hue: our black is neutral (R-B = 3/255 against the reference's 2/255) and our red's hue angle is 5.4 deg against 4.5. Neither hue is the problem; both values are.
corrections_to_earlier_passes: V1's tag is 616.1 x 1378.9 px, aspect 0.4468 - 0.43% off the shipped card, not 0.03%. A threshold sweep from 0.25 to 0.80 of the paper level moves the aspect by only 0.13%, so the 622.0 x 1385.8 px figure reported elsewhere is not reproducible.
The flame emblem does NOT already match. Its bounding box does (to 0.45 mm), which is what an earlier pass compared; its ink is +61% and it is one welded component where both guides show five.
Our border rule insets are NOT 0.5-0.8 mm wrong. Measured against the exact atlas card origin they are within 0.15 mm of V1 on every side.

The corner chamfer is 8.05 mm, not 8.6 mm. A departure-threshold method over-measures the bevel; fitting a line to the bevel and intersecting it with the two edges gives 8.10 (V1) and 7.97 (V2), matching the ink pass's 8.09 / 7.96.
The ring's 'outer diameter 60.7 mm' conflated the two axes of an ellipse. The ring is 52.08 x 59.27 mm at mid-stroke (h/w 1.138) with a red ink extent of 58.17 x 64.82 mm.

Ring stroke width: 4.84 mm by the swept-band definition used here and by the typography pass (4.67 mm). The 6.15 mm figure elsewhere is an alpha-profile definition that includes the soft shoulder, and the 5.31 mm figure a third threshold. They are not interchangeable; the build target and the acceptance test must use the same one.
The centre glyph is in FIVE pieces, not four: body, radical, an orphan flick, and TWO strokes broken out of the body.
Our ring is not 'solid all the way round' (an ink fill of 1.01 is not a physical quantity). By stroke-envelope hole fraction it is 0.122 against the reference's 0.198 - about 60% as broken.

provenance.verification_pass: Blender 5.2.0 LTS headless, factory startup, NumPy, four scripts run for this document: tag detection and levels; ring / glyph / flame / rules / columns / seals / centreline; tolerance-free bevel fit, ink outside the rule rectangle, tight seal boxes, ring envelope holes; and the debug overlay.
provenance.legal: Nothing in this specification is derived artwork. It contains positions, sizes, fractions, angles, counts, densities and colour values measured from the guides, and descriptions of shape in words. No crop, mask, trace, outline or threshold of either guide exists anywhere a build can read.
